text:
The Sabres have now won three straight, and Tage Thompson put the capper on this one. His second goal, a snap shot on the power play at 13:40 of the third, broke a 2-2 tie and sent BUF to a 3-2 win in Los Angeles. Thompson, drafted 26th overall by St. Louis in 2016 out of UConn, finished with eight shots on goal.

The goals came in an odd order, because the Kings (LAK) played the better game. Our numbers give LAK a 66 percent chance of winning a replay of this one, the share of simulated reruns of every shot that the team takes. LAK outshot BUF in attempts 81 to 62, won 34 of 53 faceoffs and made 3.21 expected goals (the quality of the chances) to the Sabres' 2.34. The second period was lopsided, 1.65 to 0.68, yet Thompson's 5 percent chance in that period was the one that went in and made it 2-0. Corey Perry cut it to 2-1 on the power play, Andre Lee tied it early in the third, and Perry's nine shots on goal could not find a lead.

The reason was Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen. He stopped 27 of 29 and saved 1.2 goals more than the chances against him deserved. Anton Forsberg was 0.7 goals worse than expected at the other end. BUF was 2 for 3 on the power play, LAK 1 for 5, and the Sabres blocked 30 shots to the Kings' 19. That left BUF at three straight wins, while LAK, outplayed on the scoreboard despite owning the chances, has little to take from a game it controlled and still lost.
